data: The socio-cultural construction of the body is intrinsic to the constitution of the self. The body does not just define the ‘self’ but also the ‘other’ or ‘non-self’. The body is a source of knowledge while understanding social positioning and is understood through everyday living. Beauty is closely connected to the body. It is defined in terms of the perfect body and bodily appearances. In fact societies have been obsessed with a beautiful body for long. The body is a strong communicator and has a specific political anatomy of its own. It can see and is also constantly seen by the others. The course will look at the body from a political perspective and navigate through questions like what constitutes the body and how we see them. It will help in understanding the process of othering that constantly takes place in the socio-economic-political-cultural milieu we inhabit. By taking the body as the source of intervention, the course will engage with questions of self, identity, subjectivity and objectification. Thus, engaging with the sociological construction of the body, politics of visibility or that of seeing and be seen, heightened presence of technology, bodies as embodiment of caste, religion, space and disability becomes unavoidable and pivotal. It opens up the domain of alternative narratives that make us look at the body as made up of a plurality and multiplicity of bodies. The course will draw from articulations and conversations that have already been initiated by scholars like Judith Butler, Michel Foucault, Erving Goffman, Bryan Turner etc to enrich the discourse on body politics.
